# vetr.dev

> Small browser tools. Those listed here can also be driven programmatically: each has one JSON-in, JSON-out function, `submit(request)`, which its web page, a `window.<Name>` object in that page and a command-line script all share. The script runs in plain Node 22 with no install unless its entry says otherwise.

Each entry links the tool's API description: request and result schema, errors, and a worked example.

## Tools with an API

- [Forecast Calibration](https://vetr.dev/forecast-calibration/api.md): compare stated probabilities with binary outcomes; calibration plot against simulated calibrated worlds, Monte Carlo p-values for calibration error and log loss. Page: https://vetr.dev/forecast-calibration/ ; browser: `window.ForecastCalibration` ; CLI: `node forecast-calibration/cli.mjs request.json`
- [Sankey Diagrams](https://vetr.dev/sankey/api.md): Sankey diagrams from data tables (wide, long, link list, crosstab), flow matrices or a saved project; returns the project as JSON, exports SVG, PNG or an R bundle. Page: https://vetr.dev/sankey/ ; browser: `window.SankeyApp` ; CLI: `node sankey/scripts/render.cjs request.json diagram.svg` (not plain Node: it drives headless Chromium through Playwright, so it needs `npm ci` and `npx playwright install chromium` in `sankey/` first; errors are plain text)
- [Text in Image](https://vetr.dev/text-in-image/api.md): write a text inside the shape of an image (PNG pixels in); lines wrapped to the shape, letters coloured from the image, size iterated until the text fills it; returns glyph positions and colours, exports SVG. Page: https://vetr.dev/text-in-image/ ; browser: `window.TextInImage` (its `submit` returns a Promise; it runs in a worker) ; CLI: `node text-in-image/cli.mjs request.json --svg fill.svg` (`image` may be a PNG path there)
- [Crossword Generator](https://vetr.dev/crossword/api.md): crosswords from answers and clues, optionally shaped like a target picture (mask or RGBA pixels; PNG on the CLI); greedy layout then MCMC refinement, scored by the same seven penalty terms as the R generator; returns trimmed grids, numbered across/down entries and the terms, and draws SVG. Page: https://vetr.dev/crossword/ ; browser: `window.Crossword` (its calls return promises, as the page runs the search in a Web Worker) ; CLI: `node crossword/cli.mjs request.json`
- [Raster to Vector](https://vetr.dev/raster-to-vector/api.md): turn a raster image (RGBA pixels in; PNG on the CLI) into an SVG of flat-colour regions with smooth outlines; weighted k-means colours with k by Davies-Bouldin, marching-squares or original tracer, wavelet / Fourier / Hadamard smoothing, containment paint order; same SVG as the R version for the same request; returns palette, regions in paint order and the SVG. Page: https://vetr.dev/raster-to-vector/ ; browser: `window.RasterToVector` (its `submit` returns a Promise; it runs in a worker) ; CLI: `node raster-to-vector/cli.mjs --image in.png --svg out.svg` or `node raster-to-vector/cli.mjs request.json`
- [Statistical Intuitions](https://vetr.dev/intuitions/api.md): a gallery of interactive figures, one statistical idea each, behind one `submit({entry, params})` that returns `{entry, params, result}`; entries `zscore-outliers` (pooled vs stratified z-score outlier removal for two normal groups: exact share of each group removed by each rule, and a sweep over one parameter) `threshold-model` (discrete traits from a hidden normal liability: category and contingency-table probabilities, seeded samples, and the two-step polychoric fit of a table) and `correlation-geometry` (correlations as angles between unit arrows: the cone of fixed correlation, the cosine-rule range of a third correlation, the equicorrelation and one-pair-at-0 limits, and the feasible interval of one entry of a PSD correlation matrix given the rest, with expected interval widths). Page: https://vetr.dev/intuitions/ ; browser: `window.Intuitions` on every gallery page ; CLI: `node intuitions/cli.mjs request.json`
- [Name Tags](https://vetr.dev/name-tags/api.md): lay out names, one per tag, in the cells of a laser-cut tray (a preset, a regular grid or explicit cell centres); each two-line name is fitted around a decoration (DNA helix, Hershey script with an EKG trace, or none) by BFGS with restarts, as the R version does with the same seeds, or a sheet of logos is drawn instead; returns the fits and one SVG per tray-full at 96 units per inch. Page: https://vetr.dev/name-tags/ ; browser: `window.NameTags` (its calls return promises, as the page fits in a Web Worker) ; CLI: `node name-tags/cli.mjs request.json --out dir` (names, tray and logos may be file paths there)
